name: opportunity
paper_title: The Opportunity challenge: A benchmark database for on-body sensor-based activity recognition
authors: Ricardo Chavarriaga, Hesam Sagha, Alberto Calatroni, Sundara Tejaswi Digumarti, Gerhard Troster, Jose del R. Millan, Daniel Roggen
notes: 4 subjects x (5 ADL runs + 1 Drill run) in a sensor-rich kitchen. Only the 5 body-worn Xsens IMUs are converted (BACK, RUA, RLA, LUA, LLA); the 12 loose accelerometers, shoe, object and ambient sensors are not. Column offsets come from the release's own dataset/column_names.txt. UNITS RESOLVED BY MEASUREMENT: column_names.txt documents the accelerometer as MILLI-G (round(original / 9.8 * 1000)) — verified, a still IMU reads 1001.8 milli-g — but leaves the gyroscope 'unit = unknown' with round(original * 1000). Measured: the forearm gyroscope during LABELLED WALKING reaches p99 = 3151, i.e. 3.15 rad/s once divided by 1000; as deg/s that would be 3.2 deg/s for a swinging forearm, which is not physically possible. Both channels are therefore scaled by 1/1000, to g and rad/s. LABELS: the Locomotion track (stand/walk/sit/lie), NOT the 17-class ML_Both_Arms gesture track. Measured: gesture instances have a median duration of 2.6 s against a 6 s analysis window, so a window majority vote over them returns the null class almost everywhere. That cell is reported unsupported rather than forced. 15,063 dropout samples interpolated and 24 longer holes split.
